newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY'S SIMPLIFIED PRIVATISATION NEARS ITS END.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY'S SIMPLIFIED PRIVATISATION NEARS ITS END.

text.p: Hungary's state privatisation agency APV Rt is satisfied with the one-year old process of simplified privatisation and regards the program's deadline maintainable, an APV official said on Tuesday.

"APV regards this privatisation technics successful," APV's deputy managing director Imre Ragats told a news conference. "The end-1996 deadline, given by the law, can be met," he said. However, some deals, may be completed only in 1997, he added.
APV launched the simplified privatisation process in September 1995 with the aim of selling small- and medium-sized companies to investors offering the highest bid.
In two rounds of tenders, APV has generated around 4.5 billion forints of revenues, APV said in a statement.
APV had planned to generate four to six billion forints of the program, Ragats said, adding that based on concluded agreements the six billion was a realistic revenue target.
Of the included 121 companies APV has sold 72, six of them to foreign investors, Ragats said.
The total share capital of the 121 companies amounts to 22 billion forints and APV had an average of 80 percent stake in them, the statement said.
